ships.title: Tiny Freighter
ships.detail: TINY FREIGHTER, starter cargo shuttle. Compact rounded rectangular single cargo pod with a small wedge-shaped cockpit perched ahead of it and two stubby engine nacelles at the lower corners. One large unmistakable cargo bay, small working space truck, width about 60 percent of length. Simple memorable silhouette, visibly humble and nimble.

ships.title: Small Freighter

Exposed gap between center spine and containers, width about 65 percent of length. Functional workhorse, distinct from a single-pod shuttle.

ships.title: Large Freighter
ships.detail: LARGE FREIGHTER, heavy commercial twin-keel carrier. Distinctive elongated CATAMARAN silhouette: two parallel thick cargo keels holding stacked boxy container banks, connected by a bridge across their forward quarter and a rear engine yoke; obvious elongated negative space down the middle. Small forward command nose extends above the bridge. Four industrial thrusters. Width about 70 percent of length. Substantial but not an enlarged shuttle.

Short lateral crane outriggers folded against flanks, width about 78 percent of length. Many tiny scale cues convey large vessel but keep main shapes clean. ships.title: Bulk Freighter
ships.detail: BULK FREIGHTER, largest deep-space supercarrier for raw materials. Very LONG EXPOSED INDUSTRIAL TRUSS down center with a tiny pointed command module at nose, FIVE paired banks of enormous oblong mineral silos and rectangular cargo cages flanking the spine, separate wide rear reactor and eight-engine drive block. Width about 50 percent of length. Multiple lattice connections and tiny maintenance gantries provide monumental scale, but containers remain clean readable shapes. An immense cargo train in space, not a combat capital ship.
